inspections.finding: The bet retains its readable dagesh and broad baseline. A nearly vertical lower extension has a shallow middle thickening and a terminal bulb, but no uniquely separable two-node, single-node or bar/stem anatomy survives. The nearby printed bet-sheva shapes in bemachshchei and bevateihem are similarly joined neutral comparisons, not proof of this point. Literal bet hiriq and tsere plus detached qamats and same-font sheva show plausible fused alternatives. Retain the vowel disclosure without asserting source absence.

The nun has a broad diagonal foot and one rounded downward continuation. Same-page nidchu and nivhalu provide matching joined lower bulbs; literal nun hiriq can attach to the foot, while the nun qamats control carries a head and lower stem that could merge into the same opaque mass. Literal nun sheva also shows how the upper node may join the foot. The target does not resolve those classes, so retain its vowel note.

The pe has a saturated lower letter mass and a narrow descending extension ending in one bulb. Literal pe sheva shows two levels under its baseline, whereas the target has no independently identifiable upper node; a merged upper node or a different vowel head absorbed into the baseline remains possible. The same-page nefashot pe also has an opaque pointed foot and is treated as a neutral shape, not as a source of the missing vowel. Retain the exact note.

The zayin shaft narrows before a broad transverse lower mass and a further lower bulb. Same-page kizroach and literal yizafu supply true vertical sheva controls, but the fresh same-chapter zarach and zarua zayin-qamats controls have the same broad upper mass plus descending lower lobe. The target upper mass is broad enough that a stemmed head competes directly with two merged vertical nodes. Literal hiriq, patah and unpointed zayin fix the other classes but do not defeat sheva versus qamats. Retain rather than selecting a vowel from expected spelling.
